question: Should this maintainer-only landing change wait for trusted live GitHub auto-merge enablement proof, or may maintainers accept the remaining mutation-path risk based on tests and CLI contract inspection?
rationale: Repository policy treats landing automation and exact-head guards as sensitive, while the author states a real repository enablement run was intentionally deferred until the wrapper is trusted.

options.title: Require live trusted proof
options.body: Land only after a redacted real-repository run shows the verified prepared head being armed for auto-merge and the expected post-mutation state.

options.title: Accept test-and-contract proof
options.body: Approve based on focused tests, changed-gate CI, and GitHub CLI contract evidence while explicitly accepting that repository-level enablement was not demonstrated pre-merge.

recommendation.title: Require live trusted proof
recommendation.body: Land only after a redacted real-repository run shows the verified prepared head being armed for auto-merge and the expected post-mutation state.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied context calls this maintainer-requested work and shows this author assigned to the PR; broader ownership history could not be inspected.
